## Spec — Let tally total one project only

`wi_01M7YHSC65SJ22JSJ9CWX9VV1S` · pipeline `product_work` · passes `bsf spec check`

### Plan

Today `tally` always prints every project: `cmd/tally/main.go` reads `os.Args[1]` as an optional file path, calls `tally.Parse`, and prints one `%-20s %s` line per entry of `tally.Totals`. After this change, `tally --project NAME` prints exactly one line — NAME in the same `%-20s` column followed by `tally.Format` of that project's minutes — and a project with no matching entries prints `0h00m` instead of nothing. With no flag the output is byte-for-byte what it is today.

The selection logic goes in `internal/tally` as a new exported `ProjectTotal(entries []Entry, project string) Total` that sums the matching entries and returns `Total{Project: project, Minutes: 0}` when none match, so `cmd/tally/main.go` stays wiring only (fundamentals, "Keep `main` thin").

Decisions already made, so the builder has none left:

- Standard-library `flag` only — `flag.NewFlagSet("tally", flag.ContinueOnError)`, `fs.SetOutput(os.Stderr)`, one `fs.String("project", "", ...)`, parsed from `os.Args[1:]`. No new dependency.
- `flag` accepts `--project NAME`, `-project NAME` and `--project=NAME` alike (verified by experiment).
- The flag counts as set when its value is non-empty, so `--project=""` behaves as no flag.
- Project-name matching is exact and case-sensitive, as `Totals`' map keying already is.
- The file path is `fs.Arg(0)`; further positional arguments are ignored, exactly as `os.Args[1]` ignores them today.
- `Parse` still reads the whole timesheet when `--project` is given, so a malformed line anywhere is still `tally: line N: ...` and exit 1 — never a filtered zero.
- On a `fs.Parse` error, exit 1 without printing a second message; `flag` has already written its own message and usage to stderr.
- `flag` stops at the first non-flag argument, so `tally --project site sheet.txt` works and `tally sheet.txt --project site` does not. That is stock `flag` behaviour, left as is rather than hand-rolled.

`cmd/tally` has no test file and reports 0.0% of statements, while the coverage guardrail asks 80% on changed lines — so the changed lines in `main.go` would have nothing to count. `main.go` is therefore reshaped into `func run(args []string, stdin io.Reader, stdout, stderr io.Writer) int` with `func main() { os.Exit(run(os.Args[1:], os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr)) }`, and a new `cmd/tally/main_test.go` covers `run`. That is the minimum needed to make the new argument handling testable at all, not a general refactor. The README and every doc comment other than `cmd/tally/main.go`'s own usage block are untouched.

### Files the builder may touch

| File |  |
| --- | --- |
| `internal/tally/tally.go` | add `ProjectTotal` |
| `internal/tally/tally_test.go` | add two tests (declared in `tests_changed`) |
| `cmd/tally/main.go` | the flag, the `run` extraction |
| `cmd/tally/main_test.go` | new |

Feature folders: `internal/tally`, `cmd/tally`.

### Acceptance checks

1. Build, then `printf '2026-11-20 site 1h30m\n2026-11-20 docs 45m\n2026-11-21 site 2h\n' | ./tally --project site` → stdout is exactly one line, `site` in the 20-character column followed by `3h30m`; `docs` appears nowhere; exit 0.
2. `printf '2026-11-20 site 1h30m\n2026-11-20 docs 45m\n' | ./tally --project nope` → exactly one line, `nope` + `0h00m` — not empty, not an error; exit 0.
3. No flag: the runbook's Verify step 1 command still prints `site 3h30m` then `docs 0h45m`, and the CI smoke grep `^site *1h30m$` over `go run ./cmd/tally` still exits 0.
4. `printf '...' > /tmp/ts.txt && ./tally --project docs /tmp/ts.txt` → the single line `docs` + `0h45m`, exit 0. The flag works on the file route as well as stdin.
5. `printf '2026-11-20 site 1h\n2026-11-21 docs ninety\n' | ./tally --project site` → stdout empty, stderr `tally: line 2: "ninety" is not a positive duration like 1h30m`, exit 1. Naming a project does not suppress a malformed line in a different project.
6. `go vet ./... && go test ./...` pass, and `go test ./... -cover` reports above 80.0% for `cmd/tally` instead of `[no test files]`.

### Tests added

`internal/tally/tally_test.go`: `TestProjectTotalSumsOnlyTheNamedProject`, `TestProjectTotalIsZeroForAProjectWithNoEntries`.

`cmd/tally/main_test.go` (new): `TestRunWithProjectFlagPrintsOnlyThatProject`, `TestRunPrintsZeroForAProjectWithNoEntries`, `TestRunWithoutProjectFlagPrintsEveryProjectLargestFirst`, `TestRunReportsAMalformedLineOnStderrAndExitsOne`, `TestRunReadsTheFileNamedByThePositionalArgument`.

### Research the plan rests on

- `cmd/tally/main.go:15` — no `flag` import exists anywhere; all argument handling is these ten lines, so `--project` is a genuinely new surface.
- `internal/tally/tally.go:59` — `Totals` keys a `map[string]int` on `Entry.Project`, so a project with no entries has no row. That is why an unknown name needs its own function rather than a filter over `Totals`' output.
- `internal/tally/tally.go:78` — `Format(0)` already renders `0h00m`; the requested empty-project output falls out of the existing formatter with no special case.
- `cmd/tally/main.go:32` and fundamentals, "Keep the output columnar" — `%-20s %s` is what scripts grep, so the single-project line uses the same format string.
- fundamentals, "Where logic lives" / "Keep `main` thin" — a condition about timesheet content belongs in `internal/tally`, hence `ProjectTotal`.
- fundamentals, "Prefer extending `Parse`'s vocabulary over adding a flag" — a flag needs a deliberate decision; the request makes it by name. Exactly one flag, standard library, no general configuration surface.
- `ran: cd /tmp/gh-aw/agent/scratch/flagexp && go run main.go` — a `ContinueOnError` FlagSet with one `project` string flag over eight argument vectors confirmed the one-vs-two-dash equivalence, `--project=NAME`, the stop-at-first-non-flag rule, and that an undefined flag or missing value returns an error rather than exiting.
- [https://pkg.go.dev/flag](https://pkg.go.dev/flag) — package overview ("Command line flag syntax") and the `ErrorHandling` constants confirm the same for the toolchain in use.
- `ran: go test ./... -cover` — `cmd/tally` 0.0%, `internal/tally` 90.0%, against `diff_min_pct: 80` in `.factory/guardrails/coverage.json`.
- `.factory/sandbox/manifest.json` — `capabilities.exercised` covers building, `go vet`/`go test`, and running the binary on stdin and a file argument while reading stdout, stderr and exit status; that is exactly what the six checks need and nothing more. The `cmd/tally/main.go` entry in `not_exercised` states a change there will need a test added alongside it.
- fundamentals, "Product intent" and runbook Verify step 2 — a quietly wrong total is worse than none, so `--project` must not become a way to skip validation.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the smoke step pipes a two-entry timesheet with no arguments and greps `^site *1h30m$`; `.github/workflows/**` is protected by policy, so the no-flag path must stay byte-identical. Check 3 re-runs that grep.
- `internal/tally/tally_test.go:18` and fundamentals, "Test naming" / "How a test asserts" — test names are the sentence the test proves; `t.Fatalf` with the actual value, no assertion library.
- `.factory/definition/context/feature-map.md` — the domain lives in `internal/tally`, the executable in `cmd/tally`, import edge one way, no shared folder for a first use. Two feature folders is the minimal blast radius.
- `.factory/definition/policy.yaml:52` — `product_work` may change `code` and `tests`; all four files are Go source or test files outside every protected path.
- `.factory/definition/context/practices.md:17` — the practices table is empty, so there is no owner-stated practice to satisfy beyond fundamentals and the guardrails.

The plan is visible, not gated — the build proceeds from here.
